summary: Verified the SameSite=None cookie fix + COOKIE_BLOCKED UX for the 'session expired' bug when Samanvay is embedded in a cross-site iframe. All 6 requested scenario groups pass: (1) MAIN BUG - embedded-frame login for citizen and operator navigates into /citizen and /operations respectively; POST /api/auth/login 200, GET /api/auth/me 200, GET /api/applications 200; no non-/auth/me 401s; no 'session expired' toast; no login-error visible; Transactions nav, transaction detail open, and mutation POST /api/demo/journeys 201 all work from inside the frame (CSRF + Origin still enforced). (2) Cookie attributes verified via curl and via Playwright context: samanvay_session HttpOnly Secure SameSite=None Path=/api Max-Age=43200; samanvay_csrf non-HttpOnly Secure SameSite=None Path=/. (3) Top-level regression on 1920x1080 and 390x844: operator->/operations, citizen->/citizen, reload preserves session, sidebar logout returns to /login and clears samanvay_session cookie, invalid password shows 'Email or password is incorrect.' in login-error with no open-in-new-tab link and no expiry toast. (4) COOKIE_BLOCKED detection: route-intercepted /auth/me->401 after login keeps the user on /login, shows exact message 'Your browser did not keep the sign-in cookie in this embedded view. Open the app in a new tab and sign in there.' with data-testid='open-in-new-tab' anchor (target=_blank, href=login URL); unrouting and retrying logs in successfully. (5) Security regression: existing /app/tests/test_fetch_metadata_auth.py returns 17/17 - Origin allow-list, Fetch-Metadata login guard, and session-bound CSRF still enforced with SameSite=None cookies (evil origin -> 403 ORIGIN_DENIED; wrong CSRF -> 403 CSRF_DENIED; valid CSRF+Origin+Idempotency-Key -> 201). (6) Expired-session regression: clearing cookies and clicking a sidebar link redirects to /login with 'session has expired' toast. No app code was modified.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthProvider.login() swallows any non-401 error from the post-login /auth/me verification (try/catch throws only on 401). If /auth/me returns 5xx or a network error the user is treated as logged in with the fresh POST /auth/login response body while the app was unable to confirm the cookie roundtrip. Consider either re-throwing on any error or, at minimum, on !e?.response (network failure) so the user isn't silently sent into a session that may not persist across the next request.

backend/modules/auth.py logout() calls response.delete_cookie for samanvay_csrf without httponly=False; delete_cookie inherits FastAPI defaults for that flag but the original cookie was httponly=False. Not a functional bug (browser matches on name+path+domain to clear) but keep the flags symmetric for readability.

Cookie SameSite=None is required for the iframe-embedded use case and is guarded by Origin allow-list + Fetch-Metadata + CSRF, which is correct. Note that Chrome is progressively deprecating third-party cookies; when 3PC is blocked users will hit the COOKIE_BLOCKED path which is now handled - good defense in depth.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iframe-embedded session bug is fully fixed. Cookies now use SameSite=None; Secure. Cross-site protection is preserved by Origin allow-list, Fetch-Metadata login guard, and session-bound CSRF token in X-CSRF-Token header. The Playwright frame test uses parent origin https://example.com and iframe src pointing to the preview URL; Chromium allows 3PC by default so cookies flow. For 3PC-blocked emulation, route.fulfill /api/auth/me with 401 - AuthProvider will throw COOKIE_BLOCKED and LoginPage renders data-testid='login-error' + data-testid='open-in-new-tab'.
rca of the issue: USER RCA: After a recent change adding a global 401 axios interceptor that redirects to /login with 'session expired' toast, users experiencing the app inside a cross-site preview iframe were bounced back to /login immediately after login. The samanvay_session cookie was set with SameSite=Lax which browsers refuse to send from cross-site iframes, so the very next GET /api/applications came back 401 - the interceptor then cleared state and showed the expiry toast. FIX (already applied by main agent, verified by this iteration): backend/modules/auth.py sets both samanvay_session and samanvay_csrf with SameSite=None; Secure so they are transmitted from cross-site frames; cross-site abuse still blocked by exact Origin allow-list, Sec-Fetch-Site guard on /auth/login, and session-bound CSRF token on all mutating requests. Frontend AuthProvider.login() now does GET /auth/me right after POST /auth/login; if the browser silently dropped the cookie (e.g. Safari or Chrome 3PC-blocked profile), it throws a COOKIE_BLOCKED error which LoginPage surfaces with an 'Open in a new tab' escape hatch.
